transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... well, my brain just feels like it stalls out lately. I'm an engineering technologist, and lately I'll sit there with a test report or even just a simple CAD note open for an hour, and I just can't decide what the next sentence or checkbox should be. It's like I just can't think straight or make a decision anymore.
Along with this mental stalling, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the time?

I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed feeling sad or down, exactly. It's mostly just... well, like I said, my mind just feels completely blank. I guess I haven't really thought about it as being hopeless, I just know I'm stuck when I try to do my job.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy doing?

Yeah, I suppose I have. I usually like making things, but my 3D printer for miniatures has just been sitting there with the same half-finished figure on it for months now. And even things like doing yoga or taking a walk in the woods... it just feels like another task I have to get through instead of something I actually want to do.
Overall, about how long have you been experiencing these difficulties with your thinking and motivation?
This has been going on since I was moved into the prototype-testing role at work. So... that was about a year and a month ago.
How has your sleep been during this time?
I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't noticed any big changes with my sleep. I guess I just go to bed and wake up like normal. I haven't really been paying attention to it.
How have your energy levels been lately—have you been feeling more fatigued or wiped out than usual?

No, I don't think so. My physical energy is pretty much the same as it always is. I mean, I'm not feeling exhausted or physically wiped out... it's really just the motivation that's gone, not my actual energy.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight over this past year?
No, I haven't really noticed any changes there. My appetite is pretty much the same as always. I haven't gained or lost any weight... I just eat my normal meals.
Have you been feeling down on yourself, or having feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt?

Yeah, I have. I just keep... replaying these tiny mistakes from the lab in my head. And I end up telling myself that I'm not just bad at this job, but that I'm actually a bad person. It feels like I deserve whatever consequences come from it.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself, or that you would be better off dead?

Yeah, I have. When I'm on my commute, I catch myself thinking that it would just be easier if I didn't arrive anywhere. Sometimes the idea of just steering off the road pops into my head... and it actually scares me enough that I have to grip the steering wheel really tight and just pull over for a minute.
Have you or anyone else noticed that you are moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual, or that you feel unusually restless and fidgety?

Yeah, I've noticed it. And I think other people have, too. In meetings, people have started finishing my sentences for me because... well, it just takes me so long to get the words out. And physically, even just walking from my desk to the test chamber at work, it feels like I'm moving through thick syrup. Everything just takes so much effort.
